about: The speakers a singer's body is weighed from (src/blend.rs; research/VOCALWIND_CHOIR.md): each a VocalTractLab speaker file, its anatomy, articulatory ranges, shapes and glottis measured or made from one person. A new speaker is a file in the folder and an entry here. `learned`: files of shapes learned for a speaker beyond its own (vtl-carry-shapes' and vtl-carry-area's `out`), its vowels' added where it has none of them; a speaker without one weighs in with its nearest's (languages/ipa.json). M01's and W02's /A/ /V/ /M/ not kept: carried by their area functions, /A/ came 386 cents low at M01's first resonance, /V/ 298 low at W02's second; The /3`/ (measured [ɝ]) carried to each, then its first three resonances tuned on the engine to the measured area function's laid on the same tube (vtl-carry-area tune=yes; languages/carry.json): carried, JD2's and W02's had come 259 and 288 cents high at their first, 357 and 305 at their second; tuned, every speaker's lands within 20 cents (research/VOCALWIND_LANGUAGES.md). `match_children_by`: the attributes that tell apart a file's children of one kind (a shape by its name, a glottis's control parameter by its index, a glottis model by its type), else their order. `fossa`: a speaker's piriform fossa laid for its trough where it is measured, its volume its file's (sing-score.mjs --fossa measured, vtl-stream fossa=; none asked, the file's; a body's its speakers' weighed, none where one of them has none). The engine's fossa is one cone, whose trough falls at 12.8 kHz cm over its length (its network in frequency, examples/tract_response.rs: 6.4 kHz at 2.0 cm, 5.1 at 2.5, 3.7 at 3.5): the men's files' 2.5 cm puts it at 5.2 kHz, where the Dresden Vocal Tract Dataset's man's printed /u/ has it from 4.0 to 5.4 kHz, deepest from 4.6 to 5.0 (research-downloads/voice/dresden-vocal-tract-dataset, s1-05, its measured transfer), and sung vowels show "a pronounced dip at 4-5 kHz" (S. Ternström 2008, "Hi-Fi voice", Acoustics'08 Paris), laid to the fossae by J. Dang & K. Honda 1997 (JASA 101(1), 456-465, doi:10.1121/1.417990; to fetch). 2.75 cm puts it at 4.65 kHz; lengthened at its volume a body's first three resonances move 4 Hz at most (the bass's five Latin vowels, 17 November 2026). W02's file's 2.5 cm stands: TU Berlin's soprano's trough is deepest from 5.0 to 5.75 kHz (voices/measured-soprano.json).

JD2.source: VocalTractLab 2.4 (P. Birkholz, TU Dresden), from MRI of a native German speaker's vocal tract (VTL2.4 manual, B.1)

M01.source: VocalTractLab 2.4, from MRI of a native German speaker's vocal tract; made with T. Zhang (VTL2.4 manual, B.1 and Acknowledgments)

W02.source: VocalTractLab 2.4, from MRI of a native German speaker's vocal tract; made with T. Zhang (VTL2.4 manual, B.1 and Acknowledgments)
